lesson_title: The Catholic threat: Northern Earls, plots and Mary Queen of Scots
claim: About 450 rebels were executed — a deliberately harsh response to deter future revolt.
issue: The number of rebels executed after the Northern Rebellion is understated. Historical sources consistently put the figure at approximately 600, with Elizabeth having demanded at least 700. The figure of 450 is significantly below the scholarly consensus.
correction: Approximately 600 rebels were executed following the suppression of the Northern Rebellion (Elizabeth demanded at least 700; estimates range from 400 to over 600, with ~600 being the most widely cited figure).

lesson_title: The need for social reform: Booth, Rowntree and Liberal reforms
claim: Part 1 provided sickness benefit — 10 shillings per week for up to 26 weeks — to some 10 million workers who were ill.
issue: The 10 shillings per week rate did not apply for the full 26 weeks. Under the National Insurance Act 1911, sickness benefit was 10 shillings per week for the first 13 weeks, then reduced to 5 shillings per week for the following 13 weeks (total 26 weeks). Stating 10s/week for the full 26 weeks overstates the benefit rate and could lose marks in an exam answer.
correction: The sickness benefit was 10 shillings per week for the first 13 weeks of illness, then 5 shillings per week for the next 13 weeks (26 weeks total).
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Insurance_Act_1911; multiple sources confirm the two-tier rate structure

claim: In 1587, Drake launched a pre-emptive raid on Cadiz harbour, destroying approximately thirty Spanish ships being prepared for the Armada.
issue: The number of Spanish ships destroyed at Cadiz is slightly understated. Britannica records 33 ships destroyed; the Library of Congress source (based on Drake's own account) records 37. 'Approximately thirty' is at the low end and arguably inaccurate.
correction: Drake destroyed approximately 33–37 Spanish ships at Cadiz in April 1587 (Britannica: 33; Library of Congress: 37). 'Over thirty' would be more accurate than 'approximately thirty'.

claim: Of the approximately 130 ships that set out, only around 67 returned to Spain.
issue: The number of Armada ships returning to Spain is slightly overstated. Wikipedia and the majority of modern scholarship puts the figure at approximately 60–65 ships returning, not 67.
correction: Approximately 60–65 ships returned to Spain (Wikipedia records 'about 60 known to have reached Spain'; contemporary Spanish records cite 65 survived). 67 is slightly high.

lesson_title: Culture and fashion in Edwardian Britain
claim: Beatrix Potter published The Tale of Peter Rabbit in 1902, initially self-published after Frederick Warne accepted it the same year.
issue: The publication sequence is confused. Potter self-published a private edition of 250 copies in December 1901 (not 1902), after multiple publishers rejected the manuscript. Frederick Warne then accepted and published the first commercial trade edition in October 1902. Saying she self-published 'after' Warne accepted it 'the same year' inverts the order: she self-published first (1901), Warne published second (1902).
correction: Potter privately printed 250 copies in December 1901 after publishers rejected it. Frederick Warne & Co. then published the first commercial edition in October 1902. The self-publication preceded (and prompted) the Warne commercial deal, not vice versa.
